abstract: Amyloid fibrils formed by amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}) in Alzheimer's disease (AD) are characterized by parallel in-register (PAIR) interpeptide {beta}-sheets. Although A{beta}42 is more amyloidogenic than the more abundant A{beta}40 isoform, the familial Arctic E22G mutation disproportionately enhances the amyloidogenicity of A{beta}40, effectively reversing this relationship. To uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying this differential response, we systematically compared the monomeric conformational ensembles and dimerization dynamics of both wild-type (WT) and E22G mutant A{beta}40 and A{beta}42 using long-timescale atomistic discrete molecular dynamics simulations with enhanced sampling by replica permutation. We found that the propensity to form extended inter-peptide PAIR alignments in dimerization recapitulates the relative amyloidogenicity of the four A{beta} variants. Our results reveal an isoform-dependent balance between electrostatic frustration near residues 22-23 and the stabilizing interactions gained upon productive PAIR assembly. In WT A{beta}42, the two additional C-terminal residues promote formation of an extended conformation spanning the central hydrophobic core (CHC) and adjacent sequence. Upon PAIR alignment, the resulting backbone hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic contacts provide sufficient stabilization to compensate for unfavorable electrostatic interactions involving E22 and D23. In contrast, A{beta}40 forms shorter {beta}-strands within CHC and more frequently adopts off-register parallel or antiparallel intermolecular {beta}-sheets, making electrostatic frustration a greater barrier towards productive PAIR assembly. Neutralization of E22 by the Arctic E22G mutation therefore lowers this barrier more strongly in A{beta}40 than in A{beta}42, providing a molecular explanation for the mutation-induced reversal of their relative amyloidogenicity. Together, these results establish an isoform-dependent mechanism by which {beta}-strand preorganization modulates the impact of electrostatic frustration on early A{beta} assembly and support PAIR alignment as a structural reaction coordinate for characterizing fibril-nucleating interactions.

title: Molecular mechanisms driving the Arctic E22G-induced amyloidogenicity switch between Aβ40 and Aβ42
